title: Man vs bacteria
paragraphs: If you live in England and have a mild infection, don't ask your GP for antibiotics. He will probably refuse and give you something else instead. This is part of a drive to put a stop to harmful infections becoming resistant to these drugs.

Recent figures from the NHS have shown that the number of prescriptions for all types of antibiotics were down by 7.3% on the previous year to about 34 million in 2015 and 2016, which is considered a success by the authorities.

Peter Taylor, Professor of Microbiology, UCL School of Pharmacy, says that antibiotics are probably "the safest and most effective drugs ever produced, but they have an Achilles heel - every time we use an antibiotic it alters the levels of bacteria out there in the environment and engenders resistance in a way that is very similar to Darwinian natural selection.

The power of these substances was discovered by Alexander Fleming in 1928 almost by chance. The Scottish bacteriologist returned to his laboratory after a holiday to find a bacteria-free circle around a growth of mould on a Petri dish. It gave us our first antibiotic: penicillin.

The availability of these drugs revolutionised the treatment of infections. In the past STIs spread by bacteria were often incurable and deadly. Today all it takes to treat them is a trip to the clinic and a course of antibiotics. Childbirth was very dangerous and routinely ended in death for both mother and baby. Now the risk of a woman dying in England and Wales during labour is between 40 and 50 times lower than 60 years ago.

Bacteria will continue to evolve to seek survival and we have to up our game. There hasn't been a new class of antibiotics since the 1980s and pharmaceutical companies are looking into a wide-range of alternatives - from compounds from insects to nanotechnology - to develop new weapons in the continuous war against superbugs.

vocabulary.entry: mild infection [n.] /maɪld ɪnˈfekʃən/ 轻微感染 (医学词汇)
vocabulary.example: The doctor said it was just a mild infection.
vocabulary.translation: 医生说这只是轻微感染。

vocabulary.entry: GP (General Practitioner) [n.] /ˌdʒiː ˈpiː/ 家庭医生 (缩写)
vocabulary.example: Make an appointment with your GP if you feel unwell.
vocabulary.translation: 如果你感到不适，预约你的家庭医生。

vocabulary.entry: antibiotic [n.] /ˌæntibaɪˈɒtɪk/ 抗生素 (医学词汇)
vocabulary.example: He took antibiotics for his throat infection.
vocabulary.translation: 他因喉咙感染服用了抗生素。

vocabulary.entry: put a stop to [phr.] /pʊt ə stɒp tuː/ 制止；使停止 (固定搭配)
vocabulary.example: We must put a stop to this behaviour.
vocabulary.translation: 我们必须制止这种行为。

vocabulary.entry: resistant to [adj.] /rɪˈzɪstənt tuː/ 对……有抵抗力的 (专业词汇)
vocabulary.example: Some bacteria are resistant to antibiotics.
vocabulary.translation: 一些细菌对抗生素有耐药性。

vocabulary.entry: prescription [n.] /prɪˈskrɪpʃən/ 处方；药方
vocabulary.example: The doctor wrote a prescription for painkillers.
vocabulary.translation: 医生开了一张止痛药处方。

vocabulary.entry: down by [phr.] /daʊn baɪ/ 下降了 (表示减少的量)
vocabulary.example: Sales are down by 15 percent this quarter.
vocabulary.translation: 本季度销售额下降了15%。

vocabulary.entry: authority [n.] /ɔːˈθɒrəti/ 当局；官方 (常用复数)
vocabulary.example: Local authorities are responsible for schools.
vocabulary.translation: 地方当局负责学校事务。

vocabulary.entry: NHS (National Health Service) [n.] /ˌen eɪtʃ ˈes/ 英国国家医疗服务体系 (专有名词)
vocabulary.example: The NHS provides free healthcare in the UK.
vocabulary.translation: 英国国家医疗服务体系在英国提供免费医疗。

vocabulary.entry: microbiology [n.] /ˌmaɪkrəʊbaɪˈɒlədʒi/ 微生物学 (专业词汇)
vocabulary.example: Microbiology is the study of microscopic organisms.
vocabulary.translation: 微生物学是对微生物的研究。

vocabulary.entry: Achilles heel [n.] /əˌkɪliːz ˈhiːl/ 致命弱点 (固定搭配；典故)
vocabulary.example: His lack of patience is his Achilles heel.
vocabulary.translation: 缺乏耐心是他的致命弱点。

vocabulary.entry: alter [v.] /ˈɔːltə/ 改变；变更 (书面语)
vocabulary.example: The new plan alters the schedule completely.
vocabulary.translation: 新计划完全改变了时间表。

vocabulary.entry: bacteria [n. pl.] /bækˈtɪəriə/ 细菌 (单数: bacterium；专业词汇)
vocabulary.example: Some bacteria are beneficial to humans.
vocabulary.translation: 有些细菌对人类有益。

vocabulary.entry: engender [v.] /ɪnˈdʒendə/ 产生；引起 (书面语)
vocabulary.example: The policy engendered public opposition.
vocabulary.translation: 这项政策引起了公众的反对。

vocabulary.entry: Darwinian natural selection [n.] /dɑːˈwɪniən ˈnætʃrəl sɪˈlekʃən/ 达尔文自然选择 (专业词汇)
vocabulary.example: Darwinian natural selection explains how species evolve.
vocabulary.translation: 达尔文自然选择解释了物种如何进化。

vocabulary.entry: bacteriologist [n.] /bækˌtɪəriˈɒlədʒɪst/ 细菌学家 (专业词汇)
vocabulary.example: The bacteriologist identified the new strain.
vocabulary.translation: 细菌学家鉴定了这种新菌株。

vocabulary.entry: Petri dish [n.] /ˈpetri dɪʃ/ 培养皿 (专业词汇)
vocabulary.example: The sample was placed in a Petri dish.
vocabulary.translation: 样本被放在培养皿中。

vocabulary.entry: penicillin [n.] /ˌpenɪˈsɪlɪn/ 青霉素；盘尼西林 (医学词汇)
vocabulary.example: Penicillin was a medical breakthrough.
vocabulary.translation: 青霉素是医学上的突破。

vocabulary.entry: revolutionise [v.] /ˌrevəˈluːʃənaɪz/ 彻底改变 (英式拼写，美式: revolutionize)
vocabulary.example: The internet revolutionised communication.
vocabulary.translation: 互联网彻底改变了通信。

vocabulary.entry: STI (Sexually Transmitted Infection) [n.] /ˌes tiː ˈaɪ/ 性传播感染 (缩写；医学词汇)
vocabulary.example: STIs can be prevented with safe practices.
vocabulary.translation: 性传播感染可以通过安全行为预防。

vocabulary.entry: incurable [adj.] /ɪnˈkjʊərəbəl/ 无法治愈的 (医学词汇)
vocabulary.example: The disease was once considered incurable.
vocabulary.translation: 这种疾病曾被认为无法治愈。

vocabulary.entry: deadly [adj.] /ˈdedli/ 致命的
vocabulary.example: The snake's venom is deadly.
vocabulary.translation: 这种蛇的毒液是致命的。

vocabulary.entry: course [n.] /kɔːs/ 疗程；课程
vocabulary.example: He completed a course of physiotherapy.
vocabulary.translation: 他完成了一个疗程的理疗。

vocabulary.entry: childbirth [n.] /ˈtʃaɪldbɜːθ/ 分娩；生产
vocabulary.example: Childbirth can be a challenging experience.
vocabulary.translation: 分娩可能是一次具有挑战性的经历。

vocabulary.entry: up one's game [phr.] /ʌp wʌnz ɡeɪm/ 提升能力；提高水平 (口语；固定搭配)
vocabulary.example: To win the championship, we need to up our game.
vocabulary.translation: 要赢得冠军，我们需要提升表现。

vocabulary.entry: pharmaceutical [adj.] /ˌfɑːməˈsuːtɪkəl/ 制药的 (专业词汇)
vocabulary.example: The pharmaceutical company developed a new vaccine.
vocabulary.translation: 这家制药公司开发了一种新疫苗。

vocabulary.entry: alternative [n.] /ɔːlˈtɜːnətɪv/ 替代品；可供选择的事物
vocabulary.example: We need to find an alternative to plastic.
vocabulary.translation: 我们需要找到塑料的替代品。

vocabulary.entry: compound [n.] /ˈkɒmpaʊnd/ 化合物 (化学词汇)
vocabulary.example: The compound is found in many plants.
vocabulary.translation: 这种化合物存在于许多植物中。

vocabulary.entry: nanotechnology [n.] /ˌnænəʊtekˈnɒlədʒi/ 纳米技术 (专业词汇)
vocabulary.example: Nanotechnology is used in medicine and electronics.
vocabulary.translation: 纳米技术用于医学和电子学。

vocabulary.entry: superbug [n.] /ˈsuːpəbʌɡ/ 超级细菌 (医学词汇；口语)
vocabulary.example: Superbugs are resistant to multiple antibiotics.
vocabulary.translation: 超级细菌对多种抗生素有耐药性。

sentences.english: If you live in England and have a mild infection, don't ask your GP for antibiotics.
sentences.chinese: 如果你住在英格兰，并且有轻微感染，不要让你的家庭医生给你开抗生素。

sentences.english: He will probably refuse and give you something else instead.
sentences.chinese: 他很可能会拒绝，然后给你开别的药。

sentences.english: This is part of a drive to put a stop to harmful infections becoming resistant to these drugs.
sentences.chinese: 这是一项措施的一部分，旨在制止有害感染对这些药物产生耐药性。

sentences.english: Recent figures from the NHS have shown that the number of prescriptions for all types of antibiotics were down by 7.3% on the previous year to about 34 million in 2015 and 2016, which is considered a success by the authorities.
sentences.chinese: 英国国家医疗服务体系最近的数据显示，2015年至2016年，所有类型抗生素的处方数量比上一年下降了7.3%，约为3400万张，这被当局视为一项成功的举措。

sentences.english: Peter Taylor, Professor of Microbiology, UCL School of Pharmacy, says that antibiotics are probably "the safest and most effective drugs ever produced, but they have an Achilles heel - every time we use an antibiotic it alters the levels of bacteria out there in the environment and engenders resistance in a way that is very similar to Darwinian natural selection.
sentences.chinese: 伦敦大学学院药学院的微生物学教授彼得·泰勒表示，抗生素可能是“有史以来最安全、最有效的药物，但它们有一个致命弱点——每次我们使用抗生素时，它都会改变环境中的细菌数量，并以一种与达尔文自然选择非常相似的方式产生耐药性”。

sentences.english: The power of these substances was discovered by Alexander Fleming in 1928 almost by chance.
sentences.chinese: 这些物质的功效是亚历山大·弗莱明在1928年几乎偶然间发现的。

sentences.english: The Scottish bacteriologist returned to his laboratory after a holiday to find a bacteria-free circle around a growth of mould on a Petri dish.
sentences.chinese: 这位苏格兰细菌学家度假归来后，在实验室的培养皿中发现，霉菌周围有一圈没有细菌的区域。

sentences.english: It gave us our first antibiotic: penicillin.
sentences.chinese: 这让我们有了第一种抗生素：青霉素。

sentences.english: The availability of these drugs revolutionised the treatment of infections.
sentences.chinese: 这些药物的出现彻底改变了感染的治疗方式。

sentences.english: In the past STIs spread by bacteria were often incurable and deadly.
sentences.chinese: 过去，由细菌传播的性传播感染往往无法治愈，而且会致命。

sentences.english: Today all it takes to treat them is a trip to the clinic and a course of antibiotics.
sentences.chinese: 如今，治疗这些感染只需去一趟诊所，服用一个疗程的抗生素即可。

sentences.english: Childbirth was very dangerous and routinely ended in death for both mother and baby.
sentences.chinese: 过去，分娩非常危险，常常导致母婴双亡。

sentences.english: Now the risk of a woman dying in England and Wales during labour is between 40 and 50 times lower than 60 years ago.
sentences.chinese: 现在，在英格兰和威尔士，女性在分娩时死亡的风险比60年前降低了40到50倍。

sentences.english: Bacteria will continue to evolve to seek survival and we have to up our game.
sentences.chinese: 细菌将继续进化以谋求生存，我们也必须提升自己的应对能力。

sentences.english: There hasn't been a new class of antibiotics since the 1980s and pharmaceutical companies are looking into a wide-range of alternatives - from compounds from insects to nanotechnology - to develop new weapons in the continuous war against superbugs.
sentences.chinese: 自20世纪80年代以来，就再也没有出现过新一类的抗生素了。制药公司正在研究各种各样的替代方案——从昆虫体内的化合物到纳米技术——以便在与超级细菌的持续斗争中开发出新的“武器”。
